history: The College of Business and Accountancy started its existence in 1962 with the founding of Angeles Institute of Technology. It was initially named College of Commerce with an enrollment of thirty-three (33) students. It was in July 1963 that the college was given government recognition (DECS No. 70, Series 1963) to offer the first and second year programs of the Bachelor of Science in Commerce. In 1966-67, the college graduated the first batch of five students.

The dynamism in the field of business expanded the college curricular offering, and it was in 1969 that the Department of Education granted recognition for the conferment of the degree of Bachelor of Science in Business Administration (Cert. No. GR. 150) major in Accounting, Banking and Finance, Economics, and Management and Marketing.

The expanded curricular activity changed the name of the college to College of Commerce and School for Secretaries with the integration of the Secretarial program in 1980. It was further renamed to College of Business and Economics in 1984 with the Computer Center added in the following year. In 1989, it was named College of Business Administration with the separation of the School for Secretaries and the Computer Center, the objective of which is to give these respective programs autonomy in the attainment of their respective growth potentials.

In 1992, the college was given government recognition to offer a Bachelor of Science in Accountancy. Realizing the multi-disciplinary requirements of the industry, the college offered the Bachelor of Science in Tourism Management and Bachelor of Science in Hotel and Restaurant Management in school year 2005-2006. From its humble beginning of 33 students, the College has grown into one of the largest colleges in the university.

Currently, the College of Business and Accountancy has PAASCU Level IV reaccredited status for its Business Administration Programs. The Accountancy, Hospitality Management, and Tourism Management programs are PAASCU Level III re-accredited.

Founded on the principles of democracy, academic freedom, and social responsibility, ALMAS is committed to cultivating a dynamic and empowered student community that upholds integrity, critical thinking, collaboration, and excellence. As a platform for student leadership, representation, and holistic development, it actively participates in and supports programs such as academic forums, seminars, debate competitions, legal argumentation workshops, leadership training, and networking opportunities with professionals in the legal and business sectors. Beyond campus, ALMAS engages in community extension initiatives that promote social responsibility and public service. The organization collaborates with partners in organizing legal aid outreach programs, rights awareness campaigns, and community-based initiatives aimed at improving access to basic legal knowledge and assistance. Through these efforts, ALMAS empowers its members to become competent, ethical, and socially responsive individuals, well-prepared to navigate the intersections of law, business, and governance.

studentOrganizations.name: Young Entrepreneurs’ Society – AUF Chapter (AUF-YES)

Established under the vision of YES Philippines, AUF YES is dedicated to educating, promoting, encouraging, networking, and developing aspiring and successful entrepreneurs through engagements with business leaders, learning events, mentorship, and networking opportunities. It prepares future entrepreneurs and managers by enhancing management skills and competencies, fostering self-awareness, promoting cooperation within the academic community, supporting educational initiatives, advancing learning activities within the college, and engaging in meaningful community service, ultimately shaping students into capable, values-driven leaders ready to thrive in the world of business.

programs.name: Bachelor of Science in Criminology
programs.description: The Bachelor of Science in Criminology degree program aims to produce graduates who can:
curriculum: Demonstrate technical competence and foundational knowledge in criminal law, law enforcement administration, crime detection and investigation, forensic sciences, correctional administration, and criminology research;
Perform accurate criminal detection, forensic data documentation, and specialized evidence investigation workflows using modern instrumentation aligned with legal protocols;
Execute institutional or non-institutional correctional interventions and rehabilitation programs centered on human rights and ethical accountability;
Exhibit proficient communication skills, multi-professional collaboration abilities, and professional leadership in diverse public safety agencies;
Design data-driven crime prevention programs, strategic community policing strategies, and public safety risk management frameworks; and
Uphold professional code of ethics, constitutional mandates, and civic values while striving for continuous professional development and passing the Criminologist Licensure Examination.

history: In 1979, the College of Arts and Sciences offered the Bachelor of Science in Criminology degree as one of its academic programs. It was in 1982 when the College of Criminology was established as a separate college with Prof. Jose B. Maniwang as founding dean. Under his leadership, the College of Criminology was granted recognition on June 18, 1984 by the Department of Education, Culture and Sports pursuant to DECS Order No. 23, s. 1984.

The College started with only seventy nine (79) students in 1979 and its enrolment gradually increased in the following years. It has produced a total of eight (8) topnotchers since 1990 and has graduated more than a thousand students who are now gainfully employed as law enforcement officers, laboratory technicians, signature verifiers, security officers, criminal investigators in various private and public offices in the Philippines and abroad.

Today, AUF's BS Criminology program is the only PAASCU Level 3 Reaccredited program in the country and the only Center of Excellence in Central Luzon. The AUF BS Criminology program is recognized in both regional and national levels such as Center for Human Rights Education in Region 3 and a top performing school in the February 2025 Criminologist Licensure Examination. The AUF Criminology passing rate exceeds the national average for multiple consecutive years. These awards and distinctions demonstrate the program's strong commitment to academic excellence, effective instructions, relevant and dynamic curriculum and premium laboratory equipment and facilities.
goals: Foster deep moral values, civic consciousness, and Christian values required for ethical and transparent governance in public safety and criminal justice systems;

Instill a culture of ongoing professional growth, legal excellence, adherence to human rights standards, and collaborative scientific research; and

facilities.name: Crime Scene Room
facilities.description: A specialized laboratory designed to simulate realistic mock crime scenes. It serves as an active learning center where students apply physical security techniques, secure areas, practice lifting and documentation of latent fingerprints, reconstruct crime trajectories, identify evidentiary tracking matrices, and practice real-world chain of custody processing protocols under rigorous forensic standards.

facilities.description: A fingerprint processing and archiving station. It enables students to develop competencies in camera operation, lighting, image enhancement, evidence photography, and the proper preservation of photographic records for investigative and judicial purposes.

history: The College of Education started at the time of the Angeles Institute of Technology (now Angeles University Foundation), was established on May 25, 1962 as part of the College of Arts and Sciences (CAS). It initially focused on undergraduate programs. Four years later in 1966, the Graduate School was organized. Though established as an independent unit with its own dean and support staff, the College of Education and the Graduate School co-existed, supporting and strengthening each other’s programs.

CED’s growth path would not stop. The College in Higher Education Act and aiming to upgrade the Teacher Education program through the implementation of CHED Memorandum Order (CMO) 30 series of 2004, the Commission on Higher Education (CHED) involved AUF College of Education faculty to take charge of the Region 3 capacity building and orientation on the implementation of the new Teacher Education curriculum.

The College started offering Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEEd) curriculum in 1986 and Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSE) in 1989. The AUF Integrated School, which offers elementary and high school, functions as the college’s laboratory school.

In the Academic Year 1991-1992, the two programs of the College were classified under category “A” by the DECS, Region III, a distinction awarded to very few institutions of higher learning in Central Luzon.

An administrative re-structuring was implemented in the Academic Year 1999-2000 with the introduction of the verticalized structure. The structure provided for the clustering of related programs in both graduate and undergraduate levels under one college, i.e. all the graduate programs in education were under the College of Education, the Public Administration and Business administration under the College of Business Administration and the Nursing program under the College of Nursing. The vertical structure concept for the academic disciplines was especially recommended by the CHED for universities with strong undergraduate programs.

In the Academic Year 2003-2004, the verticalized structure of the College of Education was replaced by the “old” structure. Once again, the College was made to focus on undergraduate programs. The College then offered two curricular programs. Bachelor of Elementary Education (BEEd) with six areas of concentration (English, Filipino, General Science, Mathematics, Social Studies and MAPE); Bachelor of Secondary Education (BSEd) with eight major fields (English, Filipino, Biology, Biology-Chemistry, General Science, Mathematics, Social Studies and Physical Education, Health and Music or PEHM. These curricular offerings underwent revisions based on CHED requirements and to respond better to the peculiar needs of the AUF prospective teachers.

In one of the assemblies of the CED College Parents Association (CPA), it was announced to the parents that the college would offer Chinese language Teaching (CLT) as part of the double-major program intended for BSEd. Hence in June 2010, CLT has become a tandem course of any area of specialization offered by the BSEd program in partnership with the Confucius Institute and the Fujian Normal University, People’s Republic of China. Two years after, the program prioritized having CLT paired-up with the language courses, English and Filipino. At present, CED has already produced six (6) batches of graduates who have successfully completed the double-degree program.

In June 2014, CED offered the Bachelor of Physical Education (BPE) major in School P.E cognizant to the CMO 23, series of 2011, and in June 2019, CED offered Bachelor of Special Needs Education (SNEd) degree program in line with the CMO No. 77, series of 2017.

In its quest for excellence, accrediting agencies have accorded awards to the College. These include the following: Center of Excellence for Teacher Education awarded by the Commission on Higher Education for establishing and maintaining a good record in teacher education, research and community service from 2010-2025; Center of Training School in the region as a service provider in the intensive mass training on K-12 curriculum for the in-service elementary and high school teachers of the DepEd. This recognition was given by Teacher Education Council (TEC) of the Department of Education; Partner institution, prototype teacher education syllabi developers, and developers of learning resource packages in the MATATAG curriculum of Department of Education and Philippine National Research Center for Teacher Quality; Level IV Accredited Status to both Bachelor of Elementary Education and Bachelor of Secondary Education programs as awarded by the Federation of Accrediting Agencies of the Philippines for having met the standards and the requirements of PAASCU (Philippine Accrediting Association of Schools, Colleges, and Universities); ISO 21001:2018 (International Organization for Standards) for having established and applied a quality management system for the development and provision of the academic program of CED together with the other units in the university; From a small unit in 1962 that gradually emerged as a formidable college, CED has produced topnotchers, passers in the Licensure Examination for Teachers (LET) and hundreds of graduates who are now gainfully employed as educators and education managers.

The establishment of the School earned approval from the AUF Board of Trustees on August 19, 2003 during its 56th Regular Meeting presided over by Pampanga Archbishop Paciano B. Aniceto, D.D., in his capacity as Chairman of the Board. The approval was followed by immense planning and preparation that spanned three years which included the construction of the AUF Professional Schools Building, now home to the School.

The Commission on Higher Education, upon the recommendation of the Technical Panel for Legal Education, resolved to grant AUF the permit to operate the School of Law on March 13, 2006. Under the leadership of Retired Supreme Court Justice Jose C. Vitug as Founding Dean and Atty. Domingo M. Navarro as Vice Dean, the School boasts of a roster of faculty members composed of jurists and distinguished law professors. The School is equipped with a modern law library, a moot court and state-of-the-art facilities which provide for a conducive teaching and learning environment.

The School of Law received a Certificate of Recognition from the Legal Education Board for its notable performance in the 2012, 2013 and 2014 Bar Examinations as certified by the Office of the Bar Confidant. It was listed as the top performing law school among those with 19 or less examinees. Today, the School of Law is consistently among the Top 10 law schools nationwide and the No. 1 in Northern and Central Luzon.

history: The Angeles University Foundation School of Medicine (AUF-SOM) was established in June 1983 by the authority of the Board of Medical Education and the Department of Education, Culture, and Sports with Dr. Rodolfo C. Dimayuga as founding dean, Dr. Presentacion C. Peralta as assistant dean and concurrently school secretary, and a faculty of 18, eight of whom boast of 20 years teaching experience. The AUF-SOM was initially housed in the AUF San Lorenzo Ruiz Building until it was gutted down by fire in 1993. This tragedy gave way to the construction of a new health sciences building which now houses the AUF-SOM office, lecture rooms and laboratories.

The AUF-SOM was solely affiliated with Jose B. Lingad Memorial Regional Hospital for the clinical training of students until the establishment of the AUF Medical Center on February 23, 1990. The 125-bed AUFMC is the only private tertiary teaching, training and research hospital in Central Luzon which serves as the base hospital of AUF medical and allied medical students. Acknowledged for their expertise and integrity, the AUF-SOM faculty play an active role in elevating the standards of Philippine medical education through their involvement as accreditors, technical panelists and board specialty examiners.

The AUF Doctor of Medicine program is the only PAASCU accredited program in Central Luzon. It was the first in the region given ISO 9001-2000 certification by TUV-SUD in 2008 and the only one north of Manila that is ISO 9001-2008 certified by TUV-SUD.

The AUF Doctor of Medicine program has produced outstanding board performance in the Philippine medical board exam, stellar performance at the Indian Medical Council Screening Test, and a 100% pass rate in the 2014 Nepal Medical Council Screening Test. As a result, an increased number of Indian students are now enrolled in the AUF BS Psychology program leading to the degree Doctor of Medicine.

vision: The Graduate School envisions to be the leading higher education institution in the region offering graduate programs that are responsive to the professional and executive development needs of the human resources of corporate entities and educational institutions in the private and public sectors.
mission: The AUF Graduate School aims to produce high-level professionals capable of meeting the national and international needs in the dynamic and competitive global market through the provision of graduate and continuing professional education programs anchored on advanced theories, modern technologies, best practices and current trends in the various fields.
history: In support of the University’s mission of promoting research studies and instruction in the natural and social sciences and the humanities, the Graduate School was organized during the school year 1966–1967 with an initial enrolment of 15 in the Master of Arts in Education Program. Dr. Cristian Alcantara was appointed the first Dean of the Graduate School. During the school year 1975–1976, the Doctor of Philosophy in Education major in Educational Management and the Master of Science in Mathematics programs were added to the offerings of the Graduate School. Dr. Fredeswinda Serrano, the former Vice President for Academic Affairs of Pampanga Agricultural College (PAC), was the first Ph.D. graduate of the University. After a year, the Graduate School started offering a Master’s in Business Administration.

From 1966 to the present, the Graduate School has offered the following degree programs: Ph.D. Educational Management, Ph.D. in Curriculum and Instruction, Ph.D. Public Administration, Ph.D. in Management, Doctor in Business Administration, Doctor of Public Health in Health Promotion and Education, Doctor of Information Technology, Master of Arts in Education, Master of Arts in Special Education, Master of Arts in Teaching, Master of Science in Mathematics, Master in Business Administration, Master in Public Administration, Master of Arts in Nursing, Master in Nursing, Master of Science in Information Technology, Master in Public Health, and Master of Science in Medical Laboratory Science among others.

The successful graduates of the Graduate School are regional directors of government agencies; school administrators, e.g., public school superintendents, supervisors, principals, and head teachers; government officials; businessmen, and military and police officers. It has likewise awarded honorary degrees to prominent educators, public officials, and well-known businessmen and dignitaries.

Having adopted the trimester scheme since the academic year 1983–1984, the Graduate School has been enrolling professionals including lawyers, medical doctors, engineers, accountants, executives in business and industry, public relations practitioners, and educational managers for professional growth.

In keeping faith with the University’s thrust of ensuring quality in its program offerings, the Graduate School embarked on its journey toward accreditation. On August 7–8, 2015, the Master of Arts in Education and Master in Business Administration were visited by PAASCU and were granted initial accreditation for three years, effective December 12, 2015. The same programs were visited by PAASCU on March 1–2, 2019, and were granted re-accreditation for five (5) years.

To ensure that its programs remain current and on par with the requirements set by globalization and internationalization of higher education and the new policies, standards, and guidelines of CHED, all curricula were revised and implemented effective AY 2021–2022.
Believing in the tenet that a school is only as strong as its faculty, the Graduate School continuously maintains a team of competent, experienced, and efficient faculty and administrators.

Shows adeptness in time management, leadership responsibilities, and problem-solving activities for curricular or co-curricular activities.
Collaborates harmoniously with others as a competent member of a group.
Seeks help or lends a helping hand in times of challenges.
Demonstrates grit to accomplish academic tasks or life challenges.
Accomplishes remarkable output or valuable innovative or creative work.

items.name: May Malasakit sa Kapwa or Charity as Mission — “Caritas”
bullets: To practice care and concern for others is to be charitable of one’s self; charity is self-giving love, the highest form of love (John 15:13); to love is to offer one’s self for others. The Angelenean aspires to practice charity.
Practices concern and care for others, especially the poor, the disabled and the marginalized members of society through leadership, volunteerism, service, and acts of generosity.
Initiates or participates in school-based, classroom-based, and community-based advocacies for cultural understanding, peace, respect for human rights and preservation of the environment.
Contributes time and resources for the fulfillment of the mission of the school towards community empowerment, responsible citizenship, and societal transformation.

learningOutcomes.intro: The Angeles University Foundation envisions its graduates to be responsible and competent citizens of the country and the world, imbued with the core values of “Mabuti, Magaling at May Malasakit sa Kapwa.” The Integrated School envisions its graduates to demonstrate the following outcomes:

items.title: Christ-centeredness (Aligned with “Mabuti”)
bullets: Embracing Christ’s way of life through moral living and social accountability.
Adhering to truth and Christian values amidst challenges brought about by social, political, economic and environmental crises.
Practicing fairness, honesty and integrity in all aspects of life.
Demonstrating positive disposition, maturity and courage, rooted in Catholic values, in the face of adversity.

items.title: Social and environmental responsibility (Aligned with “Malasakit sa Kapwa”)
bullets: Fosters the ethical principle that an Angelenean has an obligation to act for the benefit of the community and the environment.
Engaging in advocacies for peace, cultural heritage and the environment.
Demonstrating concern through active involvement in socio-civic activities.
Practicing tolerance for differences in race, culture, and exceptionalities.
Respecting individual dignity and human diversity.

items.title: Wisdom and academic excellence (Aligned with “Magaling”)
bullets: Demonstrating competence in various disciplines and fields of study.
Collaborating skillfully and effectively with peers, colleagues, authorities and institutions.
Demonstrating proficiency in oral and written communication using various media.
Manifesting wise decision-making, judgment and evaluation relevant to specific disciplines and academic endeavors.

items.title: Commitment to lifelong learning (Aligned with “Magaling”)
bullets: Practicing the value of further development of skills and competence in their respective fields of endeavor.
Adapting to the demands of innovation in their fields of endeavor.
Manifesting growth in moral, spiritual, socio-civic, and physical aspects of their lives.
Participating in collaborative learning for continual improvement.

items.title: Creative, innovative and critical thinking (Aligned with “Magaling”)
bullets: Demonstrating skills and competence in producing creative or innovative work, using logical and critical thinking, scientific process, and competence with the use of technology.
Analyzing and evaluating arguments and evidence logically.
Generating ideas, producing novel and useful works, methods, and approaches to solve problems.
Demonstrating competence in scientific research process and the use of technology for innovation.

items.title: Peace and universal understanding (Aligned with “Malasakit sa Kapwa”)
bullets: Underscores the importance of wisdom and academic excellence towards promoting peace and universal understanding.
Possessing national and international perspectives towards peace and universal understanding.
Demonstrating awareness, knowledge and skills when interacting effectively in culturally or linguistically diverse contexts.
Advocating peace and cultural, historical, political, environmental, and technological understanding as means of responsible citizenship in the local, national, and international contexts.
Using academic competence and technological skills in promoting Christian ideals, nationalism, environmental protection, and global understanding.
